text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were nearly unchanged late in the day after seesawing when the U.S. unemployment report sent mixed signals about the strength of the U.S. economy. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.48, down 0.19 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended a rocky day in good shape after a short squeeze in the cash market brought futures contracts back up late in the session. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-14/32, up 1/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - A combination of strong U.S. economic data, switching by investors into stocks and lingering concerns about monetary union wiped one and a half points of French bond futures this week. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.94, down 0.32 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures closed well up but below the highs of the day after taking a dive and then rebounding sharply after the release of higher-than-expected U.S. non-farm payroll data. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.59, up 0.49 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. Treasury securities remained higher at midday as investors clung to the silver lining of an ominous payrolls report. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-22/32, up 5/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.86 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond futures ended slightly lower, as it was pushed down by a flurry of position adjustment sales which appeared toward the close. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.29, down 0.08 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market business ground almost to a halt ahead of the February U.S. jobs report and the weekend. Russia, which said it planned to launch a mark Eurobond next week, may slightly delay the issue if sentiment in emerging market sector does not improve. Korea's Hanil Bank will launch a 300 million mark FRN. Among the day's activity, Commerzbank launched a 200 million pound subordinated bond at a 50 b.p. spread. Other limited activity included small deals in Austrian schillings, Danish crowns, French francs and yen.
